compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`build_server` in `src/rebar/mcp_server.py:432` constructs `mcp.server.auth.settings.AuthSettings(issuer_url=..., resource_server_url=..., required_scopes=...)` without setting `validate_token_resource`. With `mcp` 1.30.0 installed (the version in the worktree venv), every authenticated server boot emits a `DeprecationWarning` from the `_check_validate_token_resource` validator in `mcp/server/auth/settings.py`: the field is unset while `resource_server_url` is set, so it behaves as False and the library says the default becomes True in `mcp` 3.0.

Reproduced 2026-11-04 PST: `pytest tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_auth_jwks.py -W error::DeprecationWarning -k transport` fails (1 failed) with that warning raised from `settings.py:48`. No code in `src/`, `tests/`, or `pyproject.toml` sets `validate_token_resource`. Today the resource-binding behaviour is decided by a library default rather than by rebar, and the warning appears in every authenticated test run and server boot.

Primary sources: the `mcp` v1.30.0 release notes list this as a new `DeprecationWarning` ("Set it to `True` or `False`"; both keep working as before in 1.x); upstream PR modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk#3451 adds the field and states unset behaves as off. The field's own description in `settings.py` says to set it False "when your token verifier checks the token's audience itself". When True, `FastMCP.streamable_http_app()` passes `resource_server_url` to `BearerAuthBackend`, which rejects any token whose `AccessToken.resource` is not that URL (`mcp/server/auth/middleware/bearer_auth.py`, `_issued_for_this_resource`).

## Approach

Set `validate_token_resource=False` explicitly in `build_server`, with a comment naming `CompositeTokenVerifier` as the component that enforces the RFC 8707 audience. This fits because rebar's verifier already checks the audience itself: `CompositeTokenVerifier.verify_token` (`src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py:560`) accepts a sub-verifier result only when `result.resource == self._resource`, the configured `auth_resource_server_url`, and `docs/mcp-auth.md` §"The composite is the single audience / fail-closed choke point" documents it as the one place audience is enforced. False is the value the SDK prescribes for that design and is exactly today's runtime behaviour (unset already behaves as False), so no token accepted today is rejected afterwards and no token rejected today is accepted.

Correct the two statements that say the SDK bearer backend "never" inspects `.resource` (true before 1.30, now true only while `validate_token_resource` is False): the `CompositeTokenVerifier` docstring (`src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py:542`) and `docs/mcp-auth.md:79`. ADR 0050 is a dated decision record and is left unchanged.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/mcp_server.py` — pass `validate_token_resource=False` to `AuthSettings` in `build_server`, with the comment.
- `src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py` — `CompositeTokenVerifier` docstring wording only.
- `docs/mcp-auth.md` — the composite choke-point paragraph wording only.
- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_auth.py` — new regression test; set `validate_token_resource=False` on the hand-built `AuthSettings` in `test_wrong_resource_stub_verifier_401_at_transport` (line 327) so it mirrors the production wiring and stops emitting the same warning.
- `tests/unit/test_mcp_health_startup_handshake.py` — set `validate_token_resource=False` on the hand-built `AuthSettings` in `_server` (line 57), whose docstring says it mirrors how `build_server` builds the HTTP transport. `git grep -n 'AuthSettings(' -- src tests` lists exactly these three construction sites (`tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py:86` is a docstring mention, not a construction).

## Testing

- Regression (fails before the fix): a new test in `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_auth.py` builds the server via `build_server(_auth_config(...))` inside `warnings.catch_warnings()` with `filterwarnings("error", message=".*validate_token_resource.*", category=DeprecationWarning)`, then asserts `server.settings.auth.validate_token_resource is False`. Before the fix it raises the `DeprecationWarning`; after, it passes. No autouse fixture.
- Behaviour preserved: the existing transport tests still pass unchanged in assertions — `test_wrong_resource_stub_verifier_401_at_transport` (wrong-resource token is 401 via the composite), `test_http_auth_valid_token_200_and_missing_token_401` (static PAT 200, missing 401), `test_missing_required_scope_403_and_present_200`, and `test_jwt_transport_valid_200_garbage_401` in `test_mcp_auth_jwks.py` (valid JWT 200, garbage 401).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `build_server` passes `validate_token_resource=False` with a comment naming `CompositeTokenVerifier` as the audience enforcer; verified by the new regression test in `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_auth.py` passing (and failing on the pre-fix tree).
- [ ] `pytest tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_auth_jwks.py -W error::DeprecationWarning -k transport` passes (it fails with 1 failed before the fix).
- [ ] `pytest tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_auth.py tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_auth_jwks.py tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_auth_proxy.py tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py` passes.
- [ ] Every `AuthSettings(` construction sets the field: `git grep -n -A1 'AuthSettings(' -- src tests` shows `validate_token_resource=False` at `src/rebar/mcp_server.py`, `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_auth.py`, and `tests/unit/test_mcp_health_startup_handshake.py`, and `pytest tests/unit/test_mcp_health_startup_handshake.py -W error::DeprecationWarning` passes.
- [ ] The unconditional claim is gone: `git grep -n 'never inspects\|never checks' -- src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py docs/mcp-auth.md` returns no hits, and both passages instead say the SDK checks `.resource` only when `validate_token_resource` is True, which rebar leaves False.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0 with the worktree `.venv/bin` first on PATH.
- [ ] [non-codebase] The change lands through Gerrit at `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`; evidence recorded as a ticket comment: Gerrit change number, both vote outcomes, and the merged SHA.
- [ ] [non-codebase] The MCP autodeploy picks up the merged SHA and the deployed server still authenticates; evidence recorded as a ticket comment: the value of `/var/lib/rebar/mcp-deployed-sha` on the prod host (written by `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` as `MCP_SHA_FILE`), read with a read-only `aws ssm send-command --profile frontier` running `cat`, matching the merged SHA, and the outcome of one read-only MCP call made with the existing PAT (token never printed), with timestamps.
